targets.authors: Striegel-Moore RH, Wilson GT, Debar L, et al.
targets.title: Cognitive behavioral guided self-help for the treatment of recurrent binge eating.
targets.evidence_quote: This study was a replication and extension trial of our original study examining the effectiveness and cost-effectiveness of a brief guided self-help treatment for binge eating disorders in a nonspecialty health care (HMO) setting ( 23 , 39 ).
targets.outcome_quote: In summary, this study replicated and extended the findings from our earlier study ( 23 ), which demonstrated that a CBT-GSH intervention could significantly improve clinical outcomes for binge eating in a highly cost-effective manner ( 39 ).
targets.outcome_reasoning: The explicit overall replication verdict is affirmative. Smaller abstinence rates do not overturn this verdict.

reasoning: The new randomized trial re-tests the earlier clinical treatment finding. Reference 39 is its economic companion; the present trial reports service use but does not independently re-test cost-effectiveness, so it is not a separate target. PMC prints an alternative DOI for the same title, authors, journal, pages and year; PubMed and publisher identify the supplied DOI as this article.
